claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

To continue assessing your eligibility, I have a few more questions:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care, meaning does he live with you and do you contribute to his upbringing?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me and I take care of him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

**Is Alex in any of the following situations:**
- In hospital
- In residential care
- Living with someone else for part of the week

Or does he live with you full-time at home?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he's actually been in care for a little while now - about a couple of months. But he still lives with me otherwise.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex's situation.

Since Alex has been in care for a couple of months, I need to ask a few more questions to understand the circumstances:

**Is Alex's care being paid for by a local authority (council)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, the local authority placed him in care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have one more important question about Alex's care arrangement:

**Does Alex spend at least 24 hours (a full day) each week at home with you, or does he spend 2 nights in a row each week, or 7 or more days in a row at home with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't come home that regularly. He's at the care home full-time at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I just need to confirm one more thing to complete my assessment:

**Do you live in the UK, and are you either a British or Irish citizen, or do you have the right to live in the UK (for example, through settled status or a valid visa that allows access to public funds)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all the information you've provided. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- You are a British citizen living in the UK ✓
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16) ✓
- Alex has been in local authority care for about 2 months (more than 8 weeks)
- Alex does not spend at least 24 hours a week at home, nor does he spend 2 nights in a row each week or 7+ days in a row at home with you

Unfortunately, based on the rules for children in care, after 8 weeks of being in care paid for by a local authority, you are usually no longer entitled to Child Benefit. The exception to this rule is if the child spends **at least 24 hours a week at home**, or **2 nights in a row each week**, or **7 or more days in a row at home**. Since Alex is in care full-time and doesn't meet any of these exceptions, you would not currently be eligible.

However, if Alex's situation changes and he begins spending more time at home (meeting one of the exceptions above), you may be able to claim Child Benefit again. I would recommend contacting HMRC to discuss your specific circumstances.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry that the outcome isn't what you may have hoped for. To summarise:

## Child Benefit Eligibility Decision

**For Alex:** ❌ Not currently eligible

**Reason:** Although you meet the general eligibility criteria (being a British citizen living in the UK and Alex being under 16), Alex has been in local authority care for more than 8 weeks. Under the rules, Child Benefit entitlement usually ends after 8 weeks when a child is in care paid for by a local authority.

The exceptions that would allow you to continue receiving Child Benefit require that Alex spends:
- At least 24 hours a week at home, OR
- 2 nights in a row each week at home, OR
- 7 or more consecutive days at home

Since Alex is currently in care full-time and doesn't meet any of these conditions, you are not eligible at this time.

**What you can do:**
- If Alex's situation changes and he begins spending more time at home (meeting one of the exceptions above), you may become eligible again
- You should contact HMRC to let them know about Alex's circumstances and to discuss your options

I hope this helps clarify your situation. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
